headline: Bishops prayed with Trump. The White House posted it.
summary: Twelve Catholic bishops met White House staff on October 22 and were led into the Oval Office to pray with Trump. An aide posted the video. Two bishops now say they were told the meeting was private and nobody gave permission. "I wish I had been more shrewd and less simple," wrote Bishop William Joensen of Iowa. The vote is November 3.

cover_question.q: Can a prayer be a campaign ad?

cover_answer: Two bishops say theirs was, two weeks before a vote.
table_question: If a friend took a photo of you, should they ask before posting it?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Some church leaders called bishops went to visit the president and said a prayer with him. Someone who works for the president put a video of it on the internet. Two of the bishops are sad about that: they thought the visit was private, like a secret you told one person that got passed around. Nobody is in trouble.
5-7.why: A visit, a video, a secret passed around. Nobody is hurt.
5-7.why_long: This age reads a parent's face and takes one vivid feature for the whole event, so the script gives them the prayer, the video and a secret passed on, and leaves the election off the card. Expect "why are they sad about a prayer?" They did not know anyone would show it. Being shown without asking is something this age knows.

8-12.script: Twelve bishops went to the White House on October 22. They were walked into the Oval Office to pray with Trump, and an aide posted the video. Two say they were told it was private and nobody asked, two weeks before an election. A permission slip is signed before the trip, not after.
8-12.why: Meeting, prayer, video, nobody asked. The slip comes first.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out rules and whether adults keep them, so the script runs the chain: a meeting, a prayer, a video posted, nobody asked. The permission slip is the mechanism they know, and the complaint is that it was skipped. Expect "did the president do something wrong?" The White House would not say whether it asked.

13-17.script: Can a prayer be a campaign ad? Two bishops were told the prayer was private, then an aide posted the video two weeks before the midterms. The White House's reply: no president has been better for Catholics. Second: Joensen wishes he had been "more shrewd." Should he have known?
13-17.why: The bishops were used, and they walked in. Then whose fault.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: the bishops were told the prayer was private, and they walked into the Oval Office two weeks before an election. The script asks whether a prayer can be a campaign ad, then whether Joensen should have seen it coming, which he half admits. Expect "would you have gone?" Say what you would do.

5-7.q: Did the bishops do something bad?
5-7.a: No. They said a prayer. They just didn't know anyone would put it online.

8-12.q: Why does it matter that there's an election?
8-12.a: It can look like the church picking the president's side.

8-12.q: Did the White House ask first?
8-12.a: The bishops say no. The White House would not answer that question.

13-17.q: Can a prayer be a campaign ad?
13-17.a: The bishops say so. The White House answered with Trump's record.
Pew: 30% of US Catholics approve of Trump now, down from 47% in 2025.
